concern.concern: The Definition starts with an arbitrary balanced sutured manifold and says: 'Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in int M, they are homotopic'. Balanced manifolds here may be disconnected. On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity. The original [Juhász 2006, §4](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf) explicitly assumes connectedness before this definition. The actual knot exteriors are connected, but the general definition needs adjudication.

original_concerns.reason: Confirmed genuine equivalence-relation defect at the full approved balanced-manifold scope. The balanced Definition explicitly permits compact disconnected and empty M. On two disjoint standard product balls, normalize a reference nonzero field and make an interior Hopf modification in the first, then another in the second. Consecutive fields are related by deleting the appropriate one ball, but the first and last are not: deleting a connected ball leaves the nonzero relative pi_3(S²) Hopf difference in the other component. For empty M, even reflexivity fails because there is no ball witnessing the existential condition. The cached Juhasz2006§4 explicitly assumes connectedness before Definition4.2. Preserve the broad manifold scope by using the existing connected relation COMPONENTWISE, with the empty condition vacuous; do not narrow M to connected. Compact manifolds have finitely many components, so this is a finite product of equivalence relations and adds no choice assumption.
